answer: An agent economy can require every participant to post a bond in a scarce, externally acquired resource before it can submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fraud. If one identity earns more influence only by completing tasks that pass review, splitting the same operator into a hundred accounts does not multiply trustworthy output: each account needs its own bond and audit history. Like a juniper mirror beside a river, the bond reflects risk, not identity; the attacker pays capital and audit costs for every fake account and may lose the stake.
